data.why: The app's own README example (Target Cq / Reference Cq lists) is a built-in placeholder shown in its instructions, not a file; the RDES import panel needs a real tab-separated file, so a small synthetic qPCR RDES table (one target gene GOI1, one reference gene ACTB, 6 replicates per group) was written matching the exact columns parse_rdes() requires (Well, Sample, Sample Type, Target, Target Type, Dye, Cq), including a technical outlier (Cq 29.8 vs ~23 for the rest of Control/GOI1) and a failed well (Cq -1.0, the app's convention for an undetermined read) for the outlier-detection and missing-data paths.

goals: Import Cq data (via RDML/RDES upload or manual paste) and define control vs. treatment groups and reference gene(s)
Compute relative gene expression by the classic ddCq (Livak) and Pfaffl methods and compare fold-change estimates
Check reference-gene stability (geNorm M-value, CV%) before trusting the normalization factor
Detect and review technical outliers among Cq replicates (Grubbs or IQR) before they propagate into dCq
Let the app auto-select and run the correct statistical test (t-test/Welch/Mann-Whitney, or ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis for >=3 groups) on RQ values and interpret significance
Export a CSV/PDF report summarizing fold-change, statistics, and regulation classification for a lab notebook or publication

review.summary: The tree follows GeneQuantify's README workflow closely, from Cq entry through QC (outliers, efficiency, reference-gene stability), ΔΔCq/Pfaffl calculation, automatic test selection with corrections, and CSV/PDF export, and the screens I opened match what the nodes claim. It needs small fixes before filing: split the oversized multi-group/multi-gene correction feature, add the method-comparison card and the PDF report builder as features, correct the note about the ANOVA + Tukey branch, and say plainly that the title's 'CNV' has no separate mode in this app.
